clue.text: Reluctant to wade through gas in Wipers?

definitions.note: plural noun: things used for wiping

indicators.note: something wading through a substance is surrounded by it, so the gas letters close round the other piece

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control
loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: A First World War soldier at Ypres is unwilling to advance through a gas attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipers' was the British soldiers' nickname for Ypres, where gas was used in the First World War; here it simply means things that wipe, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloths are used for wiping surfaces, so they are literally wipers.

clue.text: Tablet in water brought up: children love it

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it to read from the bottom, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the tablet sits inside the water

parts.note: a pool is a body of water
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: A dissolving tablet floats up in water, and children enjoy the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns the whole assembly in this down clue, so it reads upwards; the definition is the whole closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet on a stick is a classic children's treat, so it is something kids love.

clue.text: Mystery spy is close to the rope?

definitions.meaning: the title of a famous spy thriller film, and the label for an unidentified member of the Cambridge spy ring
a cricket fielding position near the boundary, which is marked by a rope

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielding position named here stands behind the batsman on the off side, often near the boundary rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The film about Harry Lime is a spy mystery; the cricket fielder stands by the boundary rope behind the slips.

clue.text: Prominent position of trophy in modest setting

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, signalling a container
the modest word forms a setting round the trophy word, like a mount round a jewel

parts.note: slight means small or modest
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A trophy displayed in an unassuming setting is given a prominent place.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words signal the container: 'in', and 'setting', which pictures the outer word mounted round the inner like a jewel's setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight or the centre of attention is being in a prominent position.

clue.text: Pet snake's warning, ready at last to attack

parts.note: a snake warns by hissing

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a fit is an attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: A pet snake hisses a warning and is poised to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a tame animal, but it is a noun meaning a fit of sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in this old sense is a sulk or fit of peevishness, the same as a tantrum.

clue.text: Genre piece could be choral — is it?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: its first word made novel (rearranged) could give the letters of 'choral is it'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a piece in some musical genre might be choral.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word of the answer is read as an anagram signal acting on the first word, and that rearrangement spells 'choral is it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of fiction set in the past belongs to a recognised literary genre.

clue.text: From desert islands, has turned up in the north

indicators.note: in a down entry the north is the top, so this piece goes above the islands
in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone from desert islands has appeared in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses HAS to SAH; 'in the north' puts it at the top of the down entry, above ARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to or coming from the great desert of North Africa.

clue.text: Get a good reception for symphony

definitions.meaning: to ... is to be treated well, to get on successfully
Haydn's Symphony No. 45 has this nickname, as the players leave one by one

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to do well; as one it names Haydn's famous symphony.

clue.text: Raising glasses, cheering successful entrapment operation?

definitions.meaning: drinking a health with lifted glasses
a toast cheering a police sting that worked

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as TO A STING, the toast you raise after a successful sting operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting glasses to drink someone's health is the act of drinking a toast.

clue.text: Beyond one length, flooring is in a state

indicators.note: the flooring and 'is' come beyond, that is after, the first two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
lino is linoleum floor covering

explanation.surface: Past a certain length, the flooring is in a poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests a mess; the definition is 'a state', one of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern US state, capital Springfield, is one of the fifty states.

clue.text: In spring, woman gets guide to range

indicators.note: the woman is placed inside the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: At a spa resort, a woman finds a guide to the facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is a mountain range: Himalayan guides from this people lead climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas, a Himalayan people, are famous as mountain guides and porters on expeditions.

clue.text: Given hot meal, old boy turns to tuck into wine

indicators.note: the turned piece is tucked inside the wine

parts.note: vino is informal for wine

indicators.note: turns means the old boy pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Served a spicy curry, an old boy settles into the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses only the old boy pieces, giving DALO; 'to tuck into' puts that inside the wine. 'Given' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A very spicy Indian curry is the classic hot meal on any curry house menu.

clue.text: Thick atmosphere indoors, with sub-zero weather outside

indicators.note: the weather goes outside, round the other piece

parts.note: frost forms when the temperature drops below freezing

explanation.surface: Indoors the air is stuffy while it is freezing outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A fug, a stale stuffy warm atmosphere in a closed room, is what this word denotes.

clue.text: As believer, can gain fifty converts

indicators.note: converts here is a verb: the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A believer may persuade fifty people to change their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like religious converts but is the anagram signal on CAN GAIN plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Church of England is a Christian believer of that communion.

clue.text: From star part of serial, debar a newcomer

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A star of a TV serial tries to keep out a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'From star' as the definition; 'From' is only a link, and the definition is 'star'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest star in the constellation Taurus, the eye of the bull.

clue.text: Beginning to slog to leg, against this?

definitions.text: Beginning to slog to leg, against this?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word slog is its first letter

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A batsman thinks of slogging to the leg side against this kind of bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman often slogs a slow bowler's turning ball to the leg side; the whole clue describes the bowling as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow turning bowling invites a batsman to slog across the line to leg.

clue.text: See storm devastated part of the west

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at a storm that ravaged a western region.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is an English county in the West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: This county lies in south-west England, the region the British call the West Country.

clue.text: Private sort of design for its minister?

definitions.text: sort of design for its minister?
definitions.meaning: a kind of home decoration, and the department whose minister handles home affairs

explanation.walkthrough: Many countries have a Minister of the Interior for home affairs; interior design is decorating rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner and hidden from view; also a kind of design and a government department for home affairs.

clue.text: Jug not on paving stone

indicators.note: not says the word on is left out

parts.note: a flagon is a large jug for wine or ale

explanation.surface: A jug must not be left on the paving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' tells you to remove ON from FLAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone, a flat slab laid as paving, is called this for short.

clue.text: Fish grand to include among things to eat: it is a factor

definitions.note: the answer is a kind of factor, as in the familiar phrase

indicators.note: the fish and grand pieces are included inside the food

parts.note: food is things to eat
an eel is a fish
G is an abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Adding fish to a buffet is a key consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the phrase 'the feelgood factor', a sense of optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: The feelgood factor is a stock phrase for a general sense of wellbeing and optimism.

clue.text: Old records show accountant ruined estate

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Old records show that an accountant brought an estate to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges CA with ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Early recording discs and acetate lacquer masters are known by the material they were cut on.

clue.text: 'Ad arrows in 'and, about to go across

indicators.note: about means the whole phrase is turned round

parts.note: had darts in hand means held darts, and dropping the H gives the dialect form

explanation.surface: A Cockney soldier with arrows in hand is about to cross over.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrows are darts; having them in hand is having held them, 'ELD with the Cockney dropped H. 'about' reverses 'ELD DARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle a stream or gap is to stand or stretch across it.

clue.text: Hearth covered in stone as a top

indicators.note: the hearth is covered by the stone, placed inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
an ingle is a fireside or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A hearth is built of stone as the top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is a garment: a vest-style shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn as a garment is a kind of top.

clue.text: Final direction to go before the curtain

definitions.text: Final direction to go before the curtain

parts.words: Final direction to go before the curtain
parts.note: the last stage direction in a play script, telling the actors to leave before the curtain falls

explanation.definitionFit: This Latin stage direction tells several actors to leave, often at the very end of a play.

clue.text: Persons of title show incompetence, forgetting answer

indicators.note: forgetting the answer means its letter is dropped

parts.note: to have no ability is to be incompetent

explanation.surface: Titled people show that they are useless, failing to give an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops A from NO ABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes, earls and other peers with titles make up the aristocracy as a class.

clue.text: I shall come in to knock up some soup

indicators.note: the I shall piece comes inside the other

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high in the air
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: Someone offers to drop in and make some soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock up' looks like cooking but means hitting a ball high.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilly is a thin gruel or watery soup, as served in prisons and workhouses.

clue.text: Vicar's given a twist, opening the wine

indicators.note: a twist turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the vicar's title
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: The vicar twists the corkscrew and opens the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a twist' reverses REV to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, used in martinis.

clue.text: Opportunity given to dog to prepare to run

parts.note: a turn is a chance or opportunity
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A dog given the chance gets ready to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal but is a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to turn round to flee, the moment before running away.

clue.text: Assume nothing in such a colony

definitions.text: Assume nothing in such a colony

parts.words: Assume nothing in such a colony
parts.note: assume here means put on clothing, so people who put on nothing at all live in this kind of colony

explanation.definitionFit: Naturists who wear no clothes live together in colonies named after them.
